title: Erdős #1054: σ(m)/m → ∞ Needs Only the Harmonic Series, Not Mertens
description: The parent entry (erdos-1054-oq-01) axiomatizes the analytic input σ(m)/m → ∞, attributing it to Gronwall's/Mertens' theorem (absent from Mathlib). This entry shows the divergence needs none of that machinery: via the identity σ(m)/m = ∑_{d∣m} 1/d, taking m = lcm(1,…,n) gives σ(m)/m ≥ Hₙ (the n-th harmonic sum), which already diverges in Mathlib. Hence σ(lcm(1,…,n))/lcm(1,…,n) → ∞ with 0 axioms, supplying the parent's blocking step and answering its open question 'Can Mertens/Gronwall be added to Mathlib to complete the proof?'.

overview.historicalContext:
Erdős Problem #1054 concerns f(n), the least m such that n is a partial sum of the increasing divisors of m. Erdős asked (I) whether f(n) = o(n) for all n (disproved by Tao), (II) whether f(n) = o(n) for almost all n (open), and (III) whether limsup f(n)/n = ∞ (open). The parent entry formalizes the density framework for Part II through the sigma bound f(σ(m)) ≤ m, which yields f(σ(m))/σ(m) ≤ m/σ(m) = 1/(σ(m)/m). To force this ratio to 0 one needs an explicit sequence mₙ with σ(mₙ)/mₙ → ∞. The parent attributes this to Gronwall's theorem σ(m)/(m log log m) → e^γ (Gronwall 1913) or to Mertens' theorem — analytic results not present in Mathlib 4.26 — and so axiomatizes the conclusion. The parent's open-question list includes: 'Can Mertens/Gronwall's theorem be added to Mathlib to complete the proof?'.

This entry answers that question with a sharper observation: the full strength of Mertens/Gronwall is unnecessary for the divergence. The classical abundancy identity σ(m)/m = ∑_{d∣m} 1/d, applied to mₙ = lcm(1,…,n), shows σ(mₙ)/mₙ ≥ ∑_{k=1}^n 1/k = Hₙ because every k ≤ n divides lcm(1,…,n). Since the divergence of the harmonic series is already in Mathlib, the divergence σ(mₙ)/mₙ → ∞ follows with no analytic-number-theory machinery and 0 axioms.
overview.problemStatement: Supply, with 0 axioms in Lean/Mathlib, the analytic input the parent (erdos-1054-oq-01) axiomatized: an explicit sequence of integers mₙ along which the abundancy index σ(mₙ)/mₙ tends to +∞, so that the parent's sigma bound forces f(σ(mₙ))/σ(mₙ) → 0. Show in particular that the divergence does NOT require Mertens'/Gronwall's theorem.
overview.proofStrategy: Three elementary steps. (1) Abundancy identity: over ℝ, σ(m)/m = ∑_{d∣m} (m/d)/m = ∑_{d∣m} 1/d, since d ↦ m/d permutes the divisors of m (Nat.sum_div_divisors). (2) Harmonic lower bound: for mₙ = lcm(1,…,n) every k with 1 ≤ k ≤ n divides mₙ (Finset.dvd_lcm), so {1,…,n} ⊆ divisors(mₙ) and ∑_{d∣mₙ} 1/d ≥ ∑_{k=1}^n 1/k = Hₙ; the harmonic partial sum is realized by the shifted range {i+1 : i < n} ⊆ divisors. (3) Divergence: Hₙ → ∞ (Real.tendsto_sum_range_one_div_nat_succ_atTop), and a function dominating a sequence tending to +∞ also tends to +∞ (tendsto_atTop_mono), giving σ(mₙ)/mₙ → ∞. Taking reciprocals yields mₙ/σ(mₙ) → 0.
keyInsights: The abundancy index is a sum of unit fractions: σ(m)/m = ∑_{d∣m} 1/d. This single reindexing turns a statement about sizes of divisor sums into a statement about a harmonic-type series.

Mertens/Gronwall is overkill for the divergence. The parent cites σ(m)/(m log log m) → e^γ, but only DIVERGENCE σ(m)/m → ∞ is needed for the ratio to vanish, and the ordinary harmonic series already diverges.
lcm(1,…,n) is the right explicit witness: it is divisible by every k ≤ n, so its divisor set contains {1,…,n} and its abundancy index dominates Hₙ — no superabundant/primorial number theory required.
The bound is structural, not asymptotic-constant: we never estimate σ(m) precisely, only that {1,…,n} ⊆ divisors(lcm(1,…,n)), which is immediate from the definition of lcm.
This pins down exactly what the parent's axiom needed: the liminf side of Erdős #1054 Part II (a sequence with f(n)/n → 0) is elementary; only the full density-0 statement remains genuinely open.

sections.title: Header: Divergence of σ(m)/m Needs Only the Harmonic Series
sections.summary: Module docstring: recalls the parent axiomatized σ(m)/m → ∞ along a witness sequence by citing Mertens/Gronwall's theorem (absent from Mathlib), and answers the derived open question with a sharper observation — via σ(m)/m = ∑_{d∣m} 1/d, taking mₙ = lcm(1,…,n) makes the ratio dominate the harmonic partial sum Hₙ, so divergence follows from Mathlib's existing harmonic-series divergence with zero axioms, no Mertens/Gronwall needed.
sections.mathContext: $\sigma(m)/m = \sum_{d\mid m} 1/d$; for $m_n=\mathrm{lcm}(1,\dots,n)$, every $k\le n$ divides $m_n$, so $\sigma(m_n)/m_n \ge \sum_{k=1}^n 1/k = H_n \to \infty$ by Mathlib's `Real.tendsto_sum_range_one_div_nat_succ_atTop`, replacing the parent's axiomatized Mertens/Gronwall input.

sections.title: Section I: σ and the Divergence Sequence lcm(1,…,n)
sections.summary: Defines σ(m) = ∑_{d∣m} d (matching the parent), the sequence lcmUpTo n = lcm{1,…,n}, proves lcmUpTo n > 0, and proves every k with 1 ≤ k ≤ n divides lcmUpTo n.
sections.mathContext: lcm(1,…,n) is positive (an lcm of nonzero numbers) and divisible by each k ≤ n; these two facts are everything the abundancy lower bound needs.

sections.title: Section II: The Abundancy Identity σ(m)/m = ∑_{d∣m} 1/d
sections.summary: Proves (σ m : ℝ)/m = ∑_{d∣m} 1/d by rewriting each 1/d as (m/d)/m (valid since d ∣ m) and reindexing the divisor sum via d ↦ m/d using Nat.sum_div_divisors.
sections.mathContext: The complementary-divisor bijection d ↦ m/d turns the sum of reciprocals of divisors into (∑_{d∣m} d)/m = σ(m)/m, the classical formula for the abundancy index.

sections.title: Section III: The Harmonic Partial Sum Sits Inside the Ratio
sections.summary: Proves ∑_{i<n} 1/(i+1) ≤ σ(lcmUpTo n)/(lcmUpTo n): the shifted range {i+1 : i < n} is a set of divisors of lcmUpTo n, so its reciprocal sum is dominated by the full divisor-reciprocal sum, which equals the abundancy index.
sections.mathContext: Because {1,…,n} ⊆ divisors(lcm(1,…,n)), the n-th harmonic partial sum Hₙ is one block of the larger sum ∑_{d∣lcm} 1/d = σ(lcm)/lcm.

sections.title: Section IV: σ(lcm(1,…,n))/lcm(1,…,n) → ∞ with 0 Axioms
sections.summary: Main theorem sigma_ratio_tendsto_atTop: the abundancy index along lcm(1,…,n) tends to +∞, by dominating the divergent harmonic series. Corollary f_sigma_ratio_tendsto_zero: lcm(1,…,n)/σ(lcm(1,…,n)) → 0 (the parent's blocking step), plus sigma_ratio_unbounded.
sections.mathContext: tendsto_atTop_mono lifts harmonic divergence through the lower bound; taking reciprocals gives the m/σ(m) → 0 the parent needed, completing the liminf side of Erdős #1054 Part II.

conclusion.summary: A fully verified (0 sorries, 0 axioms, no native_decide) proof, in 152 lines with 7 theorems and 2 definitions, that the abundancy index σ(m)/m tends to +∞ along the explicit sequence m = lcm(1,…,n). The argument rests on the identity σ(m)/m = ∑_{d∣m} 1/d and the fact that lcm(1,…,n) is divisible by every k ≤ n, so its abundancy index dominates the harmonic partial sum Hₙ, which already diverges in Mathlib.
conclusion.implications: This supplies, with 0 axioms, the analytic input that the parent entry (erdos-1054-oq-01) axiomatized while citing Gronwall's/Mertens' theorem, and answers its open question 'Can Mertens/Gronwall be added to Mathlib to complete the proof?': for the divergence σ(m)/m → ∞ no such machinery is required — the ordinary harmonic series suffices. Combined with the parent's sigma bound f(σ(m)) ≤ m, this yields f(σ(mₙ))/σ(mₙ) → 0 along mₙ = lcm(1,…,n), so liminf f(n)/n = 0 unconditionally. It does NOT resolve the full Erdős #1054 Part II (density 0 of {n : f(n) ≥ εn}), which remains open: density requires controlling f over almost all n, not merely along one sequence.
openQuestions: Strengthen the lower bound from divergence to a rate: σ(lcm(1,…,n))/lcm(1,…,n) ≥ log n − O(1), giving an explicit slowly-growing lower envelope for the abundancy index without the full Gronwall constant e^γ.

Formalize Mertens' third theorem ∏_{p≤x}(1−1/p)^{-1} ∼ e^γ log x (or the divergence of ∑_p 1/p) in Mathlib, which would upgrade this from one explicit sequence to the asymptotic statement underlying the full density analysis.
